description_full: Tourmaline Oil Corp. engages in the acquisition, exploration, development, and production of petroleum and natural gas properties in the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin. The company holds interests in properties located in the Alberta Deep Basin, Northeast British Columbia Montney, and the Peace River High Triassic oil complex. Tourmaline Oil Corp. was incorporated in 2008 and is headquartered in Calgary, Canada.

financial_summary: Tourmaline Oil Corp. is a large-cap energy business with a $17.2B market cap on $4.5B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -12% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -17.1pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 65% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $268M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 12.89× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -13.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.6× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 0.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 5.0% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
